content.title: About
content.content: The Mexican roll “bolillo” is a soft wheat roll traditionally used in Mexico for sandwiches and burritos. The dough is made from wheat flour, water, yeast, salt, and a small amount of sugar, then shaped into small round rolls and baked until golden. Inside they stay soft, slightly airy, and mildly sweet.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bolillo comes from the Spanish word “bolillo,” meaning a small roll.
These rolls are a staple of Mexican street food, especially in “torta” meat sandwiches.
They are often served warm so the crust stays crisp while the crumb remains soft.
In some Mexican regions butter is added to the dough for a richer flavor.
A sweet version exists, flavored with cinnamon and sugar.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Bolillo provides quickly digestible carbs that supply energy.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The traditional recipe contains little added fat, making it a light snack.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour supplies B1, B3, and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: The roll contains a modest amount of fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: Pairs well with protein
items.content: Bolillo is often used as a base for meat, fish, or bean dishes, helping to balance meals.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Bolillo contains wheat, so it is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Because of fast‑acting carbs, it can raise blood sugar quickly, which diabetics should monitor.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt is commonly added to the dough; excess intake should be limited.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the bolillo horizontally and fill it with meat, chicken, avocado, vegetables, cheese, or beans. It also works as a base for sandwiches, served with sauces, salsa, or guacamole. For extra crunch, lightly toast the roll before filling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep bolillo in a paper bag or container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, place it in an airtight bag and refrigerate for up to 5 days or freeze for up to 2 months.
